questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good reputation of Leiden University and the opportunity to live in Leiden.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great time in Leiden University, but was a bit dissapointed by how poor Leiden University handled practical things, such as signing up for courses and housing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as i joined the introduciton week called the OWL, which was both social and informaitonal.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The orientation week provided me with informaiton about studying at Leiden, other then that i did receive assistance, but it also was not neccessarry.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Incredibly difficult, I spent many months and lots of money to find housing. At one point I almost gave up on going on exchange until i got lucky on Facebook. I paid Leiden University 300 euros to find me housing, which they did not manage to until 2 weeks before my exchange (what they found was 30 minutes from Leiden and incredibly overpriced). In the meantime i had found housing on my own and i could not get the money back from Leiden University.
I reccomend to check dutch Facebook pages and not only the ones for internationals. There is many student associations in Leiden, kind of like fraternity and sororities through whch you can find housing if you're lucky, but often they don't accept non-dutch speakers. 
Seriously consider if you should go to Leiden if you do not have a plan for housing beforehand.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is almost impossible to find housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University claimed i was not qualified for several subjects, but after sending my transcript of records (again) they let me pick those subjects. So be a bit critical if they deny you.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On a website which was quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Leiden has an exhange office which you can contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 5/6 of the classes i wanted, so quite succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To be critical if they deny you from a subject that you think you're qualified for.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very proffesional and engaged lecturers, who were often practicioners at a high level of their repsective subjects.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very similar to the level at Copenhagen, however be aware of the economics classes, as i picked one with introduction in the title that was definetly not introduction level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat similar, but more lectures and less seminars. More personal with the actual proffessors, then at CPH, especially in the smaller classes which i enjoyed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Privacy and Data Protection
Cyber Law
Childrens rights
Moot court public international law
Introduction to international economics
International tax law for multinational enterprises

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The tax law and moot court courses were brilliant. I do not reccomend the economics course, if you do not know much about economics already.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The charge Leiden University took for finding lackluster housing (300 euros).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Very similar to Denmark, my housing was quite cheap compared to most in Leiden however.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A very rich student life with many organisations, and a huge sports center.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A huge sports center with tennis, rugby, football, hockey, volleyball, climbing and more. Many associations connected to the sports center, such as the tennis club Qravel which also arranges social events.
Also just social student associaitons not neccesarily connected to Leiden University such as the infamous Minerva fraternity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Should join a student association, if dutch speaking one of the dutch ones to experience the culture, but otherwise there are many associations also for international students. This is the best way to meet other people at Leiden along with sport associations.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Hague and excperience a trial at the ICC or ICJ.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, i lived with 7 dutch people and it was no problem to fit in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join an associaiton as mentioned above.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing in particular cultural, but there is quite a divide between dutch students and internationals which would have been hard to deal with if i did not live with dutch people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the humor and directness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
to engage with the student associatons or sports life
use the law library as it is beautiful
seriously consider housing before applying

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: only as already stressed that housing is incredibly difficult

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with dutch people experiencing the culture, and learning in a new way compared to Copenhagen University

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the organisaitonal abilites of Leiden University.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
